sentences.text: In default of payment of  ine, 1 month RI more.

Heard Mr. Ashok Kumar Swarnakar, learned counsel appearing for the appellant as well as Mr.
Shailendra Sharma, learned Panel Lawyer appearing for the respondent/State on the instant application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail (I.A. No. 1 of 2024).

Case of the prosecution in brief is that the appellant is alleged to have committed repeated sexual intercourse in between year 2019 to 2023 with the victim on the pretext of marriage concealing the fact that he is a married person and as such has cheated the victim.

Learned counsel for the convict/appellant has argued that the appellant has been falsely implicated in the present case and there is no evidence on record to connect the appellant with commission of the ofence.

There are no ingredients of ofence under Section 376(2)
Ravidas Mahant vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62624264/
1 (n) or Section 417 of the IPC in this case.

It is further argued by the learned counsel for the appellant that the victim is a major girl and she had made physical relationship with the appellant on her own will and she was a consenting party and was knowing fully well about the appellant and his family.

No injury was found on the body of the victim and merely on the basis of statement of the victim (PW-3), Dr. Bharti Patel (PW-6), Dr. G.S.Jatra (PW-7) and Nilam Kerketta (PW- 8), the appellant has been convicted.

The appellant was on bail during the trial and has never misused the liberty granted to him and after his conviction, he is in jail since 07.02.2024 and further, the appeal is likely to take a couple of years or even more in its inal disposal, hence he prays that the appellant be enlarged on bail.

On the other hand, Mr. Shailendra Sharma, learned Panel Lawyer appearing for the State/respondent opposes the aforesaid bail application and submits that the indings arrived at by the learned trial Court is just and proper which warrants no interference as the same is based on proper appreciation of evidence.
We have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the documents appended with the bail application.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case that the victim was a consenting party and she had established physical relationship with the appellant on her own will and no injury was found over the body of the victim and as per the allegation, the appellant made physical relationship from 2019 to 2023, but the FIR was lodged only on 02.01.2023 after a long delay for which there is no plausible explanation and further that the appellant is in jail since 07.02.2024 and further hearing of this appeal would take some time, we deem it appropriate to allow the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail moved on behalf of the appellant.
Accordingly, the substantive jail sentence awarded to appellant- Ravidas Mahant by the learned trial Court is hereby suspended.
He shall be released on bail on his executing bail bond to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court for his appearance before the Registry of this Court on 02.08.2024.

He shall thereafter appear before the concerned trial Court on a date to be given by the Registry of this Court and shall continue to appear there on all such subsequent dates as are given to him by the said Court, interval being not less than 06 months, till inal disposal of this appeal.
Consequently, I.A. No. 1 of 2024 is allowed.

It is made clear that the observations made herein above are only conined for disposal of aforesaid I.A. iled in this appeal and it shall not be construed as an expression of opinion of this Court on the merits of the matter.
List this matter for inal hearing.

Sd/- Sd/-
 (Sachin Singh Rajput) (Ramesh Sinha)
